items.title: Tree-Ising: Repairing Language Models with Bit-Level Ising Edits
items.summary: Weight-space programming, introduced in recent MIT work by Takehi et al., enables a frontier LLM agent to read a network's weights and write a repair. items.summary: Trained action policies write manipulation skill into network weights, tying what is learned to the distribution it is learned from. items.summary: External memory enables LLM agents to improve from experience by distilling trajectories of past tasks into concise lessons for new tasks. items.title: dNaViT: Discrete Codes are General-Purpose Visual Representations
items.summary: Discrete autoregressive modeling, notably through next-token prediction, has become a cornerstone of modern language models. items.title: Infrathon: Benchmarking Language Agents for Real-World, Long-Horizon AI Infra Optimization
items.summary: In this work, we study whether frontier agent can continually improve real-world AI infrastructure over long horizons. We introduce Infrathon, a benchmark of diverse, long-horizon AI infrastructure optimization tasks across different levels. items.summary: Dexterous manipulation requires rich spatial foresight over both the surrounding scene and the robot hand. Existing world-action models often acquire such predictive knowledge through explicit future prediction. items.summary: World action models jointly predict video and actions conditioned on language. items.summary: Challenging repository-level benchmarks remain limited for many programming language ecosystems, where filtering scarce candidates with ambiguous descriptions or defective tests can discard valuable engineering problems. items.title: FINCOSMOS: An Open-World Evaluation Paradigm for Agents in Finance
items.summary: Language agents increasingly work for users on the open Web, and finance is where trusting them is hardest. items.summary: This work proposes WaveGen, a fully end-to-end diffusion-based text-to-waveform framework based on Spectral Forcing, which jointly learns an internal spectral trajectory and the target waveform trajectory within a single model, enabling direct end-to-end text-to-waveform generation. items.title: ProTEUS: A mutation-resolved world model for closed-loop protein evolution
items.summary: Protein engineering requires navigating rugged fitness landscapes, where small sequence changes can produce large functional differences, but experimental screening can only sample a small fraction of sequence space. items.summary: Large language models can generate motion graphics from static images and natural language requests, but it remains difficult to evaluate how well models can follow requests that combine spatial, appearance, and temporal requirements. items.title: The Surprising Effectiveness of Deleting Weights in LLM Post-Training
items.summary: How little of a pretrained large language model (LLM) has to change for it to acquire new capabilities? items.summary: Lloyd's k-means algorithm is a long-running standard for clustering, with applications in data analysis, retrieval, quantization and data curation. items.title: Is Your Robot's Memory Just a Clock? Temporal Shortcuts in Memory-Augmented VLA Policies
items.summary: Memory-augmented vision-language-action (VLA) policies are meant to remember what happened. Many of them, however, fill memory by time: they sample frames uniformly across the episode and stamp each frame with its time step. items.summary: We present LCM-Promo, an LLM-based uplift model for promotion allocation. items.summary: As text-to-video (T2V) models are increasingly positioned as world simulators, it is essential to evaluate whether their videos conform to physical commonsense.
